data.long_meaning: One who conquers enemies and turns them into friends. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shatrughna usually hope their child will grow to embody enemy-turned-friend and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shatrughna total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

celebrity_usage: Lord Rama's elder brother in Hindu mythology
data.cultural_impact: The name Shatrughna, derived from Sanskrit words "shatru" meaning enemy and "ghan" meaning conquering, is of great significance in Hindu mythology. He is the second eldest of the famous Pancha Pandavas, the five brothers from the great Hindu epic Mahabharata. Shatrughna's name itself is symbolic of his role as a victory bringer against their enemies. Known for his exceptional skills in archery and courage, he famously handles the wings of Bhima's chariot, providing vital support in the great battle of Kurukshetra. His unique ability to turn enemies into friends is aptly showcased when he forgives and brings back Kamarchy, the wife of Bhishma, after their victory.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper spiritual level, Shatrughna's name carries profound teachings about peace, forgiveness, and the power of unity and love. His transformation of enemies into friends mirrors the core principle of many Eastern philosophies that aim for inner peace by overcoming and transcending conflict. The name urge us to turn our internal (mental, emotional, and spiritual) enemies into allies through forgiveness and understanding. Additionally, Shatrughna's role as a leader and warrior inspires us to apply the same principles in our lives, applying efforts to resolving and transforming adversities rather than holding grudges or indulging in violence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shatrughna, meaning 'hater of enemies,' is a symbol of courage and protection. In the Mahabharata, he is the younger brother of Lord Rama, known for his unwavering loyalty and strength in battle against their mutual foes.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Shatrughna is the name of the second eldest brother of Rama in the Indian epic Ramayana. The name Shatrughna carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Shatrughna continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Anita Shatrughna in Mumbai, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Shatrughna, which means "Enemy-turned-friend". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
